feature_name: Quantity Pricing (Storefront) — listing quantity, typeable quantity, live tier price, price-jump nudge
user_goal: Order exactly the quantity I want of a printed product, see the price for that quantity update as I type, and be told when buying a few more pieces is actually cheaper.
business_goal: Replace rigid pack/tier-row quantity selection with free quantity entry so no order is lost to an unavailable quantity, while the tier guide and price-jump nudge lift average order value toward the next cheaper rate.

user_journey.step: Sees a product card priced for a concrete quantity rather than a vague 'from' rate
Opens the product page, pre-filled with the advertised listing quantity
Types or steps a quantity; the per-piece rate and total reprice live
Reads the tier-rate guide and the price-jump nudge, optionally accepting the nudge
user_journey.route_or_state: PDP configurator below the price summary

user_journey.step: Adds to cart and edits the quantity again on the cart page

happy_path.action: Open the Business Cards category listing and read the quantity-priced card for Matte Finish Business Cards
happy_path.expected_result: The card renders one line '250 pcs for ₹2,250.00' via ProductPrice's listing branch, with the listing MRP '₹2,500.00' struck through and '10% off'. The old per-unit 'From ₹x' wording is gone. 250 is the admin-set listing quantity, not the product's minimum.

happy_path.action: Open the product detail page for Matte Finish Business Cards
happy_path.expected_result: The configurator's Quantity input is pre-filled with 250 — the product's effective listing quantity — and NOT the effective minimum of 100, proving the PDP opens on the quantity the card advertised rather than the cheapest orderable one.

happy_path.action: Read the range hint under the quantity input
happy_path.expected_result: 'Min 100 pcs' only, with no '· Max ...' clause, because this product's max_order_quantity is null. The internal 1,000,000 ceiling is never displayed, per spec section 1.

happy_path.action: Read the live price summary at the pre-filled listing quantity
happy_path.expected_result: '250 pcs', '₹9.00/pc' and Total ₹2,250.00, plus the per-piece MRP ₹10.00 struck with '10% off' and the line 'You save ₹250.00 on this quantity'. The total equals the card's listing price from hp-01 exactly — every option on this product has a 1.0 multiplier, so the advertised and landing prices coincide.

happy_path.action: Read the tier-rate guide chips and confirm the chip covering the current quantity is highlighted
happy_path.expected_result: Five chips: '100+ ₹12.60/pc', '250+ ₹9.00/pc', '500+ ₹6.75/pc', '1,000+ ₹4.95/pc' (with the best-value star), '2,500+ ₹4.05/pc'. Exactly one carries aria-current='true' and it is '250+', because tierForQuantity(250) is the 250 tier.

happy_path.action: Type 499 into the quantity input and wait out the 150 ms debounce
happy_path.expected_result: Price reprices live with no error state: '₹9.00/pc' (the 250 tier still covers 499) and Total ₹4,491.00 = 9.00 x 499. The highlighted chip stays '250+'.

happy_path.action: Read the price-jump nudge that appears below the tier guide
happy_path.expected_result: 'Add 1 more pc and pay ₹6.75/pc: ₹3,375.00 total (you save ₹1,116.00)' — one extra piece crosses into the 500 tier, which is cheaper in absolute total, so nextTierNudge returns its saving branch. Singular 'pc' because addQty is 1 with the default 'pcs' label.
Quantity becomes 500, the rate becomes '₹6.75/pc', Total animates to ₹3,375.00, the highlighted chip moves to '500+', and the nudge disappears because its tier has been reached.

happy_path.action: Add the configured 500 pieces to the cart
happy_path.expected_result: The CTA carries the live total ('Add to Cart · ₹3,375.00'), the item is added, and the button relabels to 'Update Cart'.

happy_path.action: Open the cart page and read the line quantity and total
happy_path.expected_result: The line shows a compact QuantityInput holding 500 with the 'pcs' suffix inside the field, and the line total ₹3,375.00 carried from the PDP.

happy_path.action: Open the cart drawer from the header and edit the quantity there
happy_path.expected_result: The drawer's compact QuantityInput holds 500; typing 1,000 and blurring reprices the line to ₹4,950.00 (the ₹4.95 tier x 1,000) immediately, and typing 5 snaps back to the minimum of 100 rather than erroring — the drawer is an independent QuantityInput consumer and must honour the same bounds and tier lookup as the cart page.

happy_path.action: Change the cart line quantity from 500 to 250 and blur
happy_path.expected_result: The line reprices immediately to ₹2,250.00 (the 250-tier rate ₹9.00 x 250) with no reload and no error — the cart edit uses the same tier lookup as the PDP.

alternate_paths.path_name: Feed / shopping-ad preselect lands on an exact quantity and price

steps.action: Open the PDP with the feed's own preselect query string at a higher quantity (?qty=1000 plus the listing offer's option ids)
steps.expected_result: The configurator initialises at 1,000 (preselection.quantity wins over listingQuantity), the summary reads '1,000 pcs', '₹4.95/pc', Total ₹4,950.00, and the '1,000+' chip is current — the advertised configuration is the one the customer lands on.

steps.action: Read the JSON-LD Product block emitted in the page head
steps.expected_result: name is 'Matte Finish Business Cards - 250 pcs' (listing quantity and unit label, not the preselected quantity) and the single Offer's price is 2250.00 — equal to the card line in hp-01 and to listing_offer.sale_price from the API.

steps.action: Open the PDP with an out-of-range preselect ?qty=7
steps.expected_result: The quantity is clamped up to the effective minimum (100) rather than honoured literally or rejected; the summary reads '₹12.60/pc' and Total ₹1,260.00.

steps.action: Step the quantity with the + and - buttons instead of typing
steps.expected_result: stepFor(min=100) is 10, so + moves to the next multiple of 10 and - to the previous, clamped at the minimum; '-' is disabled once the value reaches 100 and '+' is never disabled because there is no maximum.

steps.action: Tap the '2,500+' tier chip in the rate guide
steps.expected_result: Quantity jumps to 2,500 and Total becomes ₹10,125.00 — the guide doubles as a one-tap quantity picker.

alternate_paths.path_name: A maximum-limited product with no MRP, whose limit the admin half of this run set

steps.action: Read the Custom Die-Cut Stickers card, whose tiers carry no MRP at all
steps.expected_result: '50 pcs for ₹300.00' with NO strike-through and NO '% off' — listingMrp is null, so the discount block is correctly suppressed entirely rather than rendering ₹0.00 or 0% off.

steps.action: Open the stickers PDP and read the range hint, now that the admin half set a maximum of 1,000
steps.expected_result: Quantity pre-filled 50; hint reads 'Min 50 pcs · Max 1,000 pcs' — the max clause appears only because an admin set it, closing the admin-to-storefront loop for this feature.

steps.action: Read the stickers tier guide, whose dev-data rates are non-monotonic (50 @ ₹6, 100 @ ₹10, 250 @ ₹6)
steps.expected_result: Chips render every tier in quantity order with its own rate, including the DEARER 100 tier ('100+ ₹10.00/pc' after '50+ ₹6.00/pc'). The current chip is '50+'. Documents faithfully how the guide behaves when an admin's rates do not decrease monotonically.

steps.action: Type 99 into the stickers quantity input and confirm no nudge appears
steps.expected_result: Total ₹594.00 at ₹6.00/pc and NO nudge banner — the next tier (100 @ ₹10 = ₹1,000) is neither cheaper nor within 5% of ₹594, so nextTierNudge correctly returns null. The negative case for the nudge rule.

error_paths.trigger: Type 10 — below Matte Finish Business Cards' minimum of 100 — into the PDP quantity input
error_paths.expected_ui_response: A neutral helper line (role='status', class text-brand-orange, no icon, not destructive red) appears under the field reading 'Minimum order is 100 pcs'. The price still updates using clamp(10) = 100 and Add to Cart stays enabled — typing is guided, never a hard error.

error_paths.trigger: Blur the field while it still holds 10
error_paths.expected_ui_response: The input snaps to 100 and the helper becomes 'Adjusted to 100 pcs' for about 3 seconds, then clears.

error_paths.trigger: Type 9999 into the Custom Die-Cut Stickers quantity input, above its maximum of 1,000
error_paths.expected_ui_response: Helper reads 'Maximum order is 1,000 pcs'; on blur the value snaps to 1,000 and the helper becomes 'Adjusted to 1,000 pcs'.
The field shows empty (never 0, never an error), and the Add to Cart button relabels to 'Enter a quantity' and is disabled — the only state that blocks the CTA.

error_paths.trigger: Blur the field while it is empty
error_paths.expected_ui_response: The last valid quantity is restored and the CTA re-enables with its price label — an empty blur is never destructive.

error_paths.trigger: Type letters and then a 9-digit number into the quantity field
error_paths.expected_ui_response: Non-digits are stripped as typed and input is capped at MAX_DIGITS = 7 characters, so '123456789' becomes '1234567'; the value is then clamped on blur.

error_paths.trigger: Press Enter while an out-of-range quantity is in the field
error_paths.expected_ui_response: Enter commits exactly like a blur — the value snaps to the clamped number and the 'Adjusted to ...' helper appears; no form submit and no navigation.

edge_cases.case: Quantity typed below the lowest pricing tier but at or above min_order_quantity
edge_cases.existing_validation: lib/quantity.ts tierForQuantity() falls back to the lowest tier, mirroring the backend's find_pricing_tier
edge_cases.risk_note: Legitimate by design (spec section 1): an admin may set min below the lowest tier and those orders pay the lowest tier's rate. The storefront must not render ₹0 or a blank price.

edge_cases.case: Zustand cart store has not hydrated when a cart line renders
edge_cases.existing_validation: useMounted gate per the frontend CLAUDE.md hydration section
edge_cases.risk_note: A capture step that screenshots before hydration records the SSR default (0 items); any axe/Lighthouse numbers attached to that frame measure the wrong page.

edge_cases.case: Server clamps a cart quantity on sync and returns quantityCorrected
edge_cases.existing_validation: features/cart/store.ts applies the server's clamped quantity and shows one toast per sync
edge_cases.risk_note: Only reachable with a deliberately out-of-range persisted line or a stale client, so it is covered by unit tests rather than this capture.

edge_cases.case: Tier rates that are not monotonically decreasing (dev stickers: 50 @ ₹6, 100 @ ₹10, 250 @ ₹6)
edge_cases.existing_validation: Admin-side only — getTierPriceTypoWarnings warns the staff member in the product form; the storefront renders whatever is stored
edge_cases.risk_note: The customer sees a rate chip that goes UP with quantity, and correctly gets no nudge at 99 (100 x ₹10 is far more than 5% above 99 x ₹6). An admin data problem the storefront surfaces faithfully, not a storefront defect.

edge_cases.case: Product whose max_order_quantity is null (no limit)
edge_cases.existing_validation: effectiveBounds returns max: null; QuantityInput falls back to MAX_LINE_QUANTITY internally
edge_cases.risk_note: The range hint must omit the '· Max ...' clause entirely rather than printing 1,000,000, which the spec says is never displayed.

edge_cases.case: Quantity of exactly 1 with a custom unit label
edge_cases.existing_validation: unitNoun() returns 'pc' for qty 1 with the default 'pcs' label only
edge_cases.risk_note: Custom labels are deliberately left unpluralised (spec D9), so a label like 'boards' reads '1 boards'. Known, accepted copy limitation worth stating in the docs.

edge_cases.case: Checkout and order placement with a free-entered quantity
edge_cases.existing_validation: Backend order preview/create reject out-of-range via quantity_below_minimum / quantity_above_maximum (never clamp)
edge_cases.risk_note: Customer auth is OTP-only and the code is delivered out of band, so this capture cannot sign a customer in — coverage for this leg is unit/API only. A gap in this run, not in the feature.

gaps: Checkout, order confirmation and account-order rendering of '{qty} {unit}' cannot be captured end to end: customer login is OTP-only and this run has no way to read the delivered code. Covered by the backend and vitest suites instead.

The server-correction toast ('Quantity updated to fit the allowed range for N item(s)') needs a deliberately out-of-range persisted cart line and is not reachable through the UI; left to unit coverage.

Dev-database tier rates for Custom Die-Cut Stickers (50 @ ₹6, 100 @ ₹10, 250 @ ₹6, 500 @ ₹4, 1000 @ ₹2.5) are NOT the spec's production figures (50 @ ₹6, 100 @ ₹4, 150 @ ₹3.4, 200 @ ₹3). The 100 tier being dearer per piece than the 50 tier looks like stale dev data; the spec's '100 pcs = ₹400' illustration is therefore not reproducible here and every expectation in this plan uses the real dev values.
